name: Activity Feed
hint: Turn on Sample content and wait a few seconds: new events spring in at the top. Click the comment deck to fan it open.
description: Who did what, newest first, from your `items`: each has an actor (name, avatar or initials), a verb and target or a ready title, a timestamp, an icon or tone, an optional body and action buttons, and an unread flag. Items are grouped by day under sticky headers, times read relatively in the Theme's locale (or through your `formatTime`), clicking an item reports it, and unread items can be marked read one by one or all at once. Load more is yours to drive, and so are loading (a skeleton in the feed's own shape), empty and error with Try again. New items that arrive at the top are announced politely; with a fixed height the reader's place is kept and a "N new" pill offers the way back up, and focus never moves. The Sample content switch shows the live Fieldnote workspace: comments with quoted layers, version uploads with a draggable before/after wipe, status pills that morph, deploys that build to Live, runs of comments that collapse into a deck of cards, filters, ticking timestamps and rolling reaction counts.
intents: live activity feed for a team workspace
recent activity stream with comments and uploads
collapse similar notifications into a stack
audit log of status changes and deploys grouped by day
new items pill when scrolled away from the top
usage: Use for the open-ended history of a shared object or workspace: who commented, uploaded, approved or paid, newest first. Pass `items` first (each with a stable `id`, an `actor`, a `verb` and `target` or a `title`, and a `timestamp`). Add `onItemClick` to open an item, `onMarkRead` when you track unread, and `onLoadMore` + `hasMore` + `loadingMore` for older items. Own the data states with `loading`, `error` + `onRetry` and `emptyMessage`. Prepend new items to `items` as they arrive; give the feed a `height` so a reader who has scrolled down keeps their place. For a fixed sequence of steps (order tracking, onboarding) use Timeline; for a single passing message use a toast.

dataProps.description: The activity, newest first, as plain objects with a stable id. `title` replaces the actor + verb + target headline; `icon` shows as a badge on the avatar (or alone without an actor); `busy` on an action shows a spinner and blocks repeat clicks.
